categories.main_business_segments: Kusuri no Aoki Holdings operates primarily in the neighborhood retail sector, focusing on drugstores that sell pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, daily necessities, food, and operate dispensing pharmacies. The group also includes supermarket operations through subsidiaries and has recently expanded into home center retailing. Its business is organized as a single segment centered on retailing health, beauty, daily life, food, and pharmacy products.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company's core operational methods include the development and management of large-scale drugstores (150-500 tsubo) with a wide assortment of products, often co-located with dispensing pharmacies. It emphasizes efficient store operations, dominant area strategies, and supply chain optimization, including joint procurement and logistics partnerships. There is no mention of proprietary technology or manufacturing, as the business is retail-focused.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kusuri no Aoki targets local consumers seeking convenient access to pharmaceuticals, health and beauty products, daily necessities, and food. Its customer base includes families, elderly individuals, and working adults, with a particular focus on communities in regional and suburban areas. The company also serves patients requiring prescription medications through its in-store and standalone pharmacies.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates 953 stores as of May 2024, with a dominant presence in the Hokushinetsu region (Ishikawa, Toyama, Fukui, Niigata, Nagano), where it holds the top market share. It is expanding in Tohoku, Kanto, Tokai, Kansai, and Shikoku regions, with stores in 24 prefectures across Japan. All operations are domestic, with no overseas business.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kusuri no Aoki is positioned at the downstream end of the supply chain as a retailer, selling directly to end consumers. It procures products from wholesalers and manufacturers and does not engage in upstream manufacturing or midstream distribution, though it participates in joint procurement and logistics alliances.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company's strategic focus is on expanding its dominant area strategy, increasing the number of stores, and enhancing one-stop shopping convenience by integrating food and drug offerings. It aims to strengthen its position as a community pharmacy, invest in human resource development (especially pharmacists and registered sellers), and promote sustainability through energy efficiency and diversity initiatives. There is no significant in-house R&D; innovation is centered on store format, operational efficiency, and service quality.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated primarily through direct sales of products (pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, daily goods, food, and prescription drugs) to consumers at physical stores. Additional revenue comes from dispensing pharmacy services and, to a lesser extent, from supermarket and home center operations. The company also operates a membership program with a point system to encourage repeat purchases.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other national drugstore chains such as Tsuruha Holdings, Welcia Holdings (Aeon Group), and other regional and national retailers. Kusuri no Aoki is a top player in the Hokushinetsu region and is actively expanding its footprint to compete with larger chains in other regions. The industry is highly competitive, with ongoing consolidation and price competition.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending May 2024, consolidated net sales reached 436.9 billion yen (up 15.3% year-on-year), with operating profit of 18.6 billion yen and net profit attributable to parent company shareholders of 12.3 billion yen. The company has shown consistent revenue growth, driven by aggressive store openings and M&A, and aims to achieve 500 billion yen in sales by FY2026. The workforce has grown to 4,735 employees (plus 6,432 part-time/temporary staff).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kusuri no Aoki differentiates itself through its dominant area strategy, offering a wide assortment of health, beauty, daily necessities, and food products in a single location, often with an in-store pharmacy for one-stop shopping. The company emphasizes community-based service, convenience, and the role of its stores as local health and wellness hubs. Its focus on integrating food and drug offerings and expanding dispensing pharmacy services enhances customer loyalty and convenience.
